transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hello, doctor. I decided to come in because I keep eating big amounts of food at night, even when I’m not really hungry at all. It has been happening quite a bit, and I felt like I needed some help to figure out why.
When this happens, are you fully awake and choosing to eat late at night, or do you wake up from sleep and eat with little memory of it afterward?

I am completely awake when this happens, usually around nine in the evening before I go to bed rather than waking up from sleep. I remember every single detail, and although I feel like I can't stop myself in the moment, I am fully conscious and end up staring at the empty dishes with a lot of shame afterward.
After these episodes, do you ever try to make up for the eating by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? Also, about how often do these episodes happen in a typical week?

No, I never do anything like throw up, use laxatives, or try to starve myself afterward to make up for the food. As for how often, it happens at least once a week, and sometimes two or three times on tougher weeks when I'm feeling really drained after volunteering at the food bank or church.

During these episodes, does it feel like you lose control and eat an unusually large amount of food within a short period, more than most people would in similar circumstances? About how long does a typical episode last?

Yes, it absolutely feels like a switch flips and I lose all control, shoveling in way more than a normal dinner—like eating half a pan of lasagna, rolls, and bowls of ice cream. I eat all of this incredibly fast, and the whole episode usually lasts for about an hour or so right before bed.
How long has this been going on—have these binge-eating episodes been happening at least once a week for 3 months or longer?

Yes, it has been going on for much longer than three months. This pattern started about fourteen months ago after my mother passed away, and it has been happening pretty steadily at least once a week since then. It feels like I've been stuck in this cycle ever since she left.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent binge-eating episodes with clear loss of control, objectively large food intake over a discrete period, rapid eating, marked shame afterward, frequency of at least weekly, and duration over 3 months. She denies compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise. The presentation is most consistent with binge-eating disorder, which is classified under ICD-10 code F50.8.
